title: Recording: Wide Prairie, I Got Up by Linda McCartney | 1973
content:
Studio Four, EMI Pathé Marconi Studios, Paris
Producers: Linda McCartney, Paul McCartney

Having just completed the Band On The Run album, Wings were keen to maintain their momentum. In late November they recorded two songs by Linda McCartney at EMI’s Paris studios.

The McCartneys recruited guitarist Jimmy McCulloch and drummer Davy Lutton for the sessions. All were driven to Dover in a Mercedes truck, and they took the ferry to Calais before being taken to the George V hotel in Paris.

Wings’ equipment was delayed in Calais. EMI Paris’s press officer Duncan Richards told them, “Ça ne fait rien,” meaning “It doesn’t matter.” The McCartneys heard this as “San ferry Anne”, which formed the basis of a new song idea.

The band were keen to record straight away. Two recording sessions took place on 21 November 1973, the first from 12.45am to 8.30am. It was the first all-nighter in the studio’s history.

The French band Les Variations were recording in an adjacent studio, working on their album Moroccan Roll, and offered to let Wings use their equipment during the first session.

Wings first worked on Linda’s song ‘Wide Prairie’, with her on vocals, Paul McCartney on bass guitar, Denny Laine on acoustic guitar, McCulloch on electric guitar, and Lutton on drums.

The song ended with an 11-minute jam, during which Linda and Paul recorded a spoken-word section. Linda: “I was in Paris, waiting for a flight, when this guy came up to me and said…” Paul: “Have you got a light?” Paul made a copy of the exchange and added it to the song’s intro.

That evening they returned to the studio and recorded ‘I Got Up’, with Linda on guide vocals, Paul on piano, McCulloch on guitar, and Lutton on drums. Paul then overdubbed organ and bass guitar, and Linda and Denny Laine added backing vocals. The final lead vocals were not recorded until 1998.
